rationale: Evidence: iteration 4 (score 663.5) and iteration 5 (score 656.8) are on a plateau. The oval is solved (20/20, about 1.8-2.0 s, max_error about 0.02). The s-bend finishes 18-19/20. The slalom fails 20/20 off-track at progress 0.32-0.35, with max_error about 0.064 and 0.4-0.45 line-loss events per run. Steering oscillation is low (0.16 on oval, 0.31 on slalom), so the robot is not jittering. Raising kp from 2.6 to 3.0 with kd 1.1 moved slalom progress only from 0.32 to 0.35 and slightly reduced s-bend finishes, so steering gain alone is near its useful limit. Moving the sensors forward and widening the array (iteration 4) also changed little, so reach and lead are not the main constraint. The remaining levers are the robot's physical agility: how fast it can change heading for alternating bends. Narrowing wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 earlier helped (iteration 3, 563.9 to 659.4), and the mass change from 0.8 to 0.6 kg was made in the same step as the array change, so its effect is not isolated. Changes: (1) wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m, for more yaw rate per unit of wheel differential and more steering authority on tight bends. (2) mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg, to cut yaw inertia (mass times (L^2+W^2)/12) so the body turns faster. (3) Sensor row moved forward from y=0.07 to y=0.08 m, the maximum allowed, to give the largest possible lead against the turning lag. Sensor x positions and weights (x/0.04) are unchanged, so the proven signal scale stays fixed. kp 3.0, kd 1.1, base_speed 1.0 and last_direction line loss are unchanged, so the gains are not retuned at the same time. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.4 with fewer off-track ends, s-bend finish at or above 0.9, and oval still about 940 to 955. Risks: a narrower track and lighter body could raise oscillation on the oval, so if oscillation exceeds about 0.4 I will raise kd. Hypotheses to test next: (a) if slalom still fails at progress about 0.35 with similar max_error, the limit is base_speed or the line-loss search, so I will test line_loss search_right or a lower base_speed on the tight bends; (b) if oscillation rises above 0.4 on the oval, kd must rise with the higher agility; (c) if completion_time on the finishing runs stays above 2.0 s, raise base_speed toward 1.2 once finish rates are reliable. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness, so that the slalom failure point and line-loss timing can be compared against iteration 5.
